channel.title: The Margin Wars | The Rulebook Wire / AU & NZ

item.title: NZ moves on commercial cards
item.description: [cost down] So what for merchants: Lower regulated commercial-card interchange is coming; confirm what your acquirer passes through. The 22 October decision introduces commercial credit-card interchange limits on Mastercard and Visa. Who: New Zealand merchants and acquirers. Effective: 2027-04-22. Official source: https://www.comcom.govt.nz/regulated-industries/projects/interchange-fee-regulation/

item.title: Scheme fees come into view
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Use the new scheme-fee disclosures to challenge unexplained line items. First quarterly aggregate fee publications by designated card networks were due for the July–September period. Who: Card networks; acquiring teams. Effective: 2026-10-30. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Acquirer fee disclosures begin
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Compare published acquirer fees with your own card mix and contract. Qualifying large acquirers must publish merchant service fee data by merchant size and card type. Who: Large acquirers and merchants. Effective: 2026-10-30. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Australia: card surcharge reset
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Recheck checkout pricing: designated card-network surcharge rules changed. eftpos, Mastercard and Visa no-surcharge rules apply from 1 October after the RBA removed its prohibition on those rules. Who: Australian merchants and acquirers. Effective: 2026-10-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/faqs/index.html

item.title: Domestic interchange: lower caps
item.description: [cost down] So what for merchants: Lower domestic interchange caps make pass-through worth checking; net merchant savings depend on your terms. Revised interchange regulation applies to domestic-issued card transactions acquired in Australia. Who: Australian acquirers and issuers. Effective: 2026-10-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Issuer compensation rules change
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Check issuer incentives against the amended compensation rules. The amended net-compensation regime starts, with transitional arrangements for 2026/27. Who: Card networks and issuers. Effective: 2026-10-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Next: prove interchange pass-through
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Ask your acquirer how the interchange reduction reached your statement. First publication of large acquirers’ interchange pass-through measures covers October–December 2026. Who: Large acquirers and merchant finance teams. Effective: 2027-01-30. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Foreign-issued cards get a cap
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Review foreign-card pricing before the new caps apply. Interchange caps extend to foreign-issued card transactions acquired in Australia. Who: Cross-border acquiring teams. Effective: 2027-04-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Merchant statements get sharper
item.description: [deadline] So what for merchants: Make sure the new statement detail reaches your reconciliation process. More statement detail is required from the first full statement period starting on or after 1 April. Who: Australian acquirers and merchants. Effective: 2027-04-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

item.title: Scheme-fee roadmap expected
item.description: [neutral] So what for merchants: Watch for the fee roadmap; it is not itself a price cap. The RBA expects a scheme-fee roadmap by 1 April; this is an expectation, not a new fee cap. Who: Card networks and acquiring teams. Effective: 2027-04-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html
